summary: This note describes Biłgoraj County, a powiat (unit of territorial administration and local government) in Lublin Voivodeship, eastern Poland. It was established on January 1, 1999, under the Polish local government reforms passed in 1998. Its seat and largest town is Biłgoraj, south of the regional capital Lublin, and it contains three other towns: Tarnogród, Józefów, and Frampol.
one_line: Biłgoraj County is a local government powiat in eastern Poland's Lublin Voivodeship, created in 1999 with Biłgoraj as its seat.
key_facts: Biłgoraj County is a powiat, a unit of territorial administration and local government, in Lublin Voivodeship in eastern Poland.
Biłgoraj County was established on January 1, 1999.
The county was established as a result of the Polish local government reforms passed in 1998.
The administrative seat and largest town of Biłgoraj County is Biłgoraj.
Biłgoraj lies south of the regional capital Lublin.
Biłgoraj County contains three other towns besides Biłgoraj.
Tarnogród lies south of Biłgoraj and is a town in Biłgoraj County.
Józefów lies east of Biłgoraj and is a town in Biłgoraj County.
Frampol lies north of Biłgoraj and is a town in Biłgoraj County.
